unresolvedReferences.description: The packet gives no Ming reign mapping. Western years come from the packet's own draft translation (Chenghua 17 = 1481, Hongzhi 12 = 1499, Zhengde 1 = 1506, Zhengde 11 = 1516); other years in the same reign are counted from those anchors. Not independently verified.

Li Fuguo and Empress Zhang are Tang figures recalled in a lecture. The packet has no Tang chronology, so they get only an upper bound (before AD 1506) from the lecture; their own dates are a research hold.
The grandmother (祖母) who dreamed of the child is taken to be Lady Cen, Wang Hua's mother (paternal grandmother), strongly inferred.
Ji Yuanheng appears here only in the chapter heading; his biography falls in a later chunk. Bounded on or after AD 1368 only.
The old crafty clerk (老黠隸) used as an informant is unnamed and not modelled as a person.

Xu Tai, Xi Yong, Liu Hui and Gui Yong (and in s0111 Qin Jin and Yang Dan) are named in Shouren's deliberately false dispatch; they are attested as named commanders, strongly inferred, but the troop movements are not claimed as fact.
Chi Zhongrong's death is strongly inferred from 諸賊入，以次悉擒戮之 after he was detained at the feast.
Zhengde 13 (1518) and 14 (1519) are counted from the draft's Zhengde 1 = 1506 anchor; the packet has no Ming reign mapping.

The journey to Qiantang and Jingkou, the return to Nanchang and the winter solstice (s0157–s0182) are dated AD 1519 as the remainder of Zhengde 14, strongly inferred from the narrative sequence; the slander, Jiuhua and later events are bounded on or after 1519 only. Shizong's accession has no year in the packet.
Shouren's father is unnamed here; the chapter's first chunk names him Wang Hua, but identity is not asserted across chunks in this local extraction.
The draft renders 珣 as 'Xing' (the surname of Xing Xun); repaired to 'Xun'.
Jiajing 6 = AD 1527 is printed in the draft; events after the twelfth month, including Shouren's death at 57 at Nan'an, are bounded on or after 1527 only, as the packet gives no later year.

The 'two Chengs' (程二子) are two unnamed Song masters; no person rows are created for them. Zhou, Xiangshan Lu, Mencius and Zhu Xi are bounded before AD 1368 as strongly inferred, with no packet chronology (research hold).
Bangxiang's surname Cen is inferred from his father Cen Meng.
弟子正憲 is rendered 'disciple' by the draft; 弟子 can also mean 'younger brother's son'. The adoptive parent-child edge holds either way; the kinship term records both readings and no repair was made.
Chengxun's younger brother (father of Xiantong) and Ji Yuanheng's two daughters (s0326) are unnamed and not given person rows; Shouren's son taught by Ji Yuanheng (s0314) is unidentified.
Longqing and Chongzhen have no years in the packet; Longqing is bounded AD 1516–1577 and Chongzhen-era events on or after 1577, from the draft's Zhengde 11 = 1516 and Wanli 5 = 1577 glosses.
